# Multi-instrument transcription with MuScriptor *To run the examples on this page, open the [audio_ai_muscriptor](agent_transcripts.md#audio_ai_muscriptor) starting point.* MuScriptor turns a mixed recording into a list of notes, each labelled with an instrument, and a MIDI file. Field shows the notes as a piano roll that plays in step with the recording, and hands them to your code as ordinary values. MuScriptor runs in its own Python environment, started separately from Field. ```diffstatic_runner {data-lang=kotlin screenshot="assets/audio_ai_muscriptor/piano_roll.png" capture="box" open-outputs="true" wait="4" padding="16" timeout="180" w="1120" h="1100" hidden=true embed=true name="elsewhere-muscriptor" alt="Real Sonic Pi waveform and MuScriptor instrument-labelled piano roll with polyphony and onset lanes"} :::static import afield.audio.engine.WavFloatArrayLoader import java.io.File val json = FieldAudioClient.json val folder = File("public/docs/assets/audio_ai_muscriptor") val preview = json.decodeFromString(File(folder, "preview.json").readText()) val wav = WavFloatArrayLoader.loadWavToFloatArray(File(folder, "source.wav").absolutePath) val sync = "docs-real-muscriptor" val source = AudioVisualizer.renderSamplesHtml( wav.samples, wav.sampleRate, options = AudioVisualizerOptions(width = 1040, waveformHeight = 130, syncGroup = sync), wavBytes = File(folder, "source.wav").readBytes(), label = "Sonic Pi recording · 8.192 seconds", ) display( "transcription", source + analysisPreviewVisualizationHtml(preview, width = 1040, height = 400, syncGroup = sync), ) ``` Listen to the recording whose notes are shown above. The notes above are MuScriptor Small's reading of an eight-second Sonic Pi recording. Instrument colours are the model's guesses; they do not establish which instruments produced the sound. The operation is `analysis.transcribe_music`, served by any of three model sizes: | Field backend | Upstream scale | Good starting point | | --- | ---: | --- | | `analysis.muscriptor.small` | about 100M parameters | quick experiments and lower-resource machines | | `analysis.muscriptor.medium` | about 300M parameters | the upstream quality/footprint compromise | | `analysis.muscriptor.large` | about 1.4B parameters | highest accuracy when GPU memory permits | All three revisions are pinned in the service. What comes back is a set of model hypotheses rather than a score; [Limits of a transcription](#limits-of-a-transcription) says how far to trust one. ## Install and start the worker MuScriptor's source code is MIT licensed. The model weights are gated under **CC BY-NC 4.0**, with additional access terms requiring the operator to have the necessary rights to the input and output. Accept the terms for the model size you intend to use on Hugging Face, then authenticate locally and start the worker. These scripts run from `services/field-audio-ai` in the Field checkout: ```diffstatic {data-lang=bash} uvx hf auth login ./scripts/run-muscriptor-worker.sh ``` The first request downloads the model. To check the worker, run its test script; with `--model` it also downloads and runs a real model: ```diffstatic {data-lang=bash} ./scripts/test-muscriptor-worker.sh ./scripts/test-muscriptor-worker.sh --model small ``` Start the ordinary API separately with `./scripts/run-api.sh`. That script points `FIELD_AUDIO_MUSCRIPTOR_URL` at `http://127.0.0.1:8769`. Device, dtype, cache location, local checkpoint overrides, and revision override variables are documented in the [worker README](https://github.com/OpenEndedGroup/field-audio-ai/blob/main/worker-environments/muscriptor/README.md). ## Transcribing a recording Never block Field's runloop with `.get()` while a transcription is running. Compose futures, update the status card from worker events, and await the durable result: ```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin} val client = FieldAudioClient() val sourcePattern = "*sonic-pi-study*" // use audio you have the rights to transcribe val sync = "muscriptor-example" client .assetByFilename(sourcePattern) .thenCompose { source -> val audio = source.representations.firstOrNull { it.role == "canonical_project" } ?: source.representations.first { it.mediaType in setOf("audio/wav", "audio/x-wav") } val duration = requireNotNull(audio.durationSeconds) val region = AssetRegion(source.id, 0.0, duration) display( "source", audio.audioVisualizerHtml( label = sourcePattern, options = AudioVisualizerOptions( width = 1100, waveformHeight = 145, initialDurationSeconds = minOf(20.0, duration), syncGroup = sync, ), ), ) client .submit( musicTranscriptionAnalysis( region, backend = MuscriptorBackend.SMALL, instruments = emptyList(), // or hard-constrain the expected instrument groups tempoDetection = MuscriptorTempoDetection.BEST_EFFORT, requestedBy = "field:my-document/transcription", ), ) .thenCompose { accepted -> :::fold job status, progress and completion display("job", fieldAudioJobStatusHtml(accepted)) client.watch( accepted.jobId, onEvent = { event -> display("job", fieldAudioJobStatusHtml(accepted, event)) }, onError = { error -> display("stream", error.message ?: error.toString()) }, ) client.awaitAnalysis(accepted) :::endfold } } .thenAccept { result -> display( "score", analysisVisualizationHtml( result, width = 1100, height = 420, syncGroup = sync, ), ) val performanceMidi = result.musicTranscriptionMidi() val quantizedMidi = result.musicTranscriptionQuantizedMidiOrNull() display( "artifacts", "performance MIDI: ${performanceMidi.id}; quantized: ${quantizedMidi?.id ?: "not produced"}", ) } .exceptionally { error -> display("error", error.cause?.message ?: error.message ?: error.toString()) null } ``` The waveform and piano roll share Field's general time bus. Playback moves the score cursor; hover, click-to-seek, wheel zoom, and drag pan work in either view and are reflected in the other. Notes are coloured by instrument group, and the lower lane shows active polyphony against onset count. To use the notes in code, `client.musicTranscription(result)` downloads the compact MessagePack artifact and returns typed `MusicTranscriptionNote` values, so ordinary Field code can filter, group, transform, or feed the recovered notes into other music systems without parsing JSON: ```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin} client.musicTranscription(result).thenAccept { transcription -> val cello = transcription.notes.filter { it.instrument == "cello" } display("cello notes", cello.joinToString("
")) } ``` ## Controls that change the transcription - `instruments`: a hard allow-list of typed `MuscriptorInstrument` values. It often improves stable attribution when the ensemble is known, and Field completion exposes the full vocabulary. For example, `listOf(MuscriptorInstrument.CELLO, MuscriptorInstrument.FRENCH_HORN)` forbids every other instrument group. - `useSampling`, `temperature`, and `cfgCoefficient`: decoding controls. Greedy decoding is the deterministic default. - `beamSize`: beam search width; one is the default. - `preludeForcing`: carries unfinished notes across each five-second chunk boundary. Leave it on unless you are trading continuity for batched throughput. - `batchSize`: values above one require `preludeForcing = false`. - `tempoDetection`: required, best effort, or off. When a grid is found, its measured model-onset correction is applied to the source-relative note timeline. - `strictEos`: turn a chunk that exhausts its token budget into a failed job rather than a warning. ## What a completed result carries - exact source asset and time range; - onset, offset, MIDI pitch, and MuScriptor instrument group for every note; - 25 Hz active-note and onset-count trajectories; - a versioned `field.audio.music-transcription.v1` MessagePack document; - performance-timed Standard MIDI; - an optional quantized-MIDI handle for future workers (not emitted by MuScriptor 0.3.0); - package, worker, model revision, checkpoint SHA-256, preprocessing, parameters, and license metadata. The note timeline is source-relative. MuScriptor's measured onset lag is removed from the NPZ and MessagePack times before Field draws them, while the correction remains recorded in result metadata. The MIDI writer applies the same correction through MuScriptor's beat-grid path, so moving the shared playhead between waveform and score does not introduce the model's small systematic lag. ## Limits of a transcription A transcription is a set of model hypotheses, not a score. Read it against the synchronized waveform and piano roll before you treat it as one. Expect the timing and many pitches to be useful, and the whole to need correcting. The instrument labels are hypotheses too. "Piano" and "bass" on an electronic source describe what the model heard, not what made the sound, and the `instruments` allow-list is the way to say so up front. MuScriptor does **not** infer velocity, so Field draws these notes at uniform opacity rather than inventing dynamics. Its tokenizer cannot represent two simultaneous notes with the same pitch and instrument. MuScriptor 0.3.0 does not expose beat quantization at all, which is why the quantized artifact above is a handle rather than a file. And the upstream authors caution that dense mixes, unusual timbres, processed recordings, and exact offsets remain difficult. See also: [Audio AI analysis](audio_ai_analysis.md) for beats and pitch, and [Short-time spectral spaces](audio_ai_spectral_embeddings.md). Upstream references: [MuScriptor repository](https://github.com/muscriptor/muscriptor) and [small-model card](https://huggingface.co/MuScriptor/muscriptor-small).

# Speech-reactive learned spaces

*To run the examples on this page, open the [audio_ai_speech_embeddings](agent_transcripts.md#audio_ai_speech_embeddings) starting point.*

A field recording of someone talking gives a beat tracker almost nothing to hold onto. What moves
in it is voice activity, vocal timbre, prosody and phonetic motion, and that is what
`analysis.embed_speech` measures. Two speech models sit behind that one operation, and which of
them you ask changes what the motion is about.

```diffstatic_runner {data-lang=kotlin screenshot="assets/audio_ai_speech_embeddings/learned_spaces.png" capture="box" open-outputs="true" wait="4" padding="16" timeout="180" w="1120" h="1100" hidden=true embed=true name="elsewhere-speech" alt="Real emotion2vec and WavLM learned phase portraits with voice activity, energy and novelty"}
:::static
import java.io.File

val json = FieldAudioClient.json
val folder = File("public/docs/assets/audio_ai_speech_embeddings")
val previews = ["emotion2vec", "wavlm_base_plus"].map {
    json.decodeFromString<AnalysisPreview>(File(folder, "$it-preview.json").readText())
}
display(
    "speech spaces",
    speechEmbeddingPreviewDashboardHtml(previews, width = 1040, phaseHeight = 220),
)
```

These are the two workers' landmark MDS views of `near_drowning.wav`. The workflow below fits
fresh t-SNE views of a selected ten-second interval from the same cached learned features.

| Backend | Bias | Useful first reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `analysis.emotion2vec` | affect, vocal texture, prosody, speaker state | where the manner and energy of speech change |
| `analysis.wavlm_base_plus` | general self-supervised speech structure | voice/timbre/phonetic motion; layer 6 is the default compromise |

Neither backend is a transcript or a sentence-meaning model. WavLM's middle and later layers can
organize phonetic structure, but spoken meaning needs a separate ASR or language embedding lane.
Both report a position in a learned speech space every 20 ms; neither reports a word.

## Start the optional worker

From the Field Audio AI checkout (or Field4's `services/field-audio-ai` submodule):

```diffstatic {data-lang=bash}
./scripts/run-speech-worker.sh
./scripts/run-api.sh
```

The speech worker listens on `127.0.0.1:8768`; the API stays on `127.0.0.1:8765`. Each model is
downloaded and loaded the first time a job asks for it. The models have their own licence terms,
separate from Field's.

## Plotting a recording

This box first reuses a previously imported content-addressed asset. If none exists, it imports
`~/Downloads/near_drowning.wav`. Then it displays the source immediately, submits both jobs,
streams progress into replaceable cards, awaits the durable results, and gives all four phase
portraits the source player's time bus.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
import java.nio.file.Files
import java.nio.file.Path
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture

val client = FieldAudioClient()
val local = Path.of(System.getProperty("user.home"), "Downloads", "near_drowning.wav")
val sync = "near-drowning-speech"
val projectionStart = 0.0
val projectionDuration = 10.0
val projectionPoolMillis = 500.0
val projectionHopMillis = 40.0 // 25 Hz: just above a 24 fps display
display("all jobs", fieldAudioJobMonitor(heightPixels = 340))

fun Box.tracked(label: String, request: ModelOperation): CompletableFuture<AnalysisResult> =
    client.submit(request).thenCompose { accepted ->
        display("$label job", fieldAudioJobStatusHtml(accepted))
        client.watch(accepted.jobId) { event ->
            display("$label job", fieldAudioJobStatusHtml(accepted, event))
        }
        client.awaitAnalysis(accepted)
    }

client
    .assetsByFilename("*near_drowning*")
    .thenCompose { matches ->
        when {
            matches.size == 1 -> CompletableFuture.completedFuture(matches.single())
            matches.isEmpty() && Files.isRegularFile(local) -> client.importWav(local)
            else -> CompletableFuture.failedFuture(IllegalStateException("cannot resolve $local"))
        }
    }
    .thenCompose { source ->
        val audio =
            source.representations.firstOrNull { it.role == "canonical_project" }
                ?: source.representations.first { it.mediaType in setOf("audio/wav", "audio/x-wav") }
        val duration = requireNotNull(audio.durationSeconds)
        val region = AssetRegion(source.id, 0.0, duration)
        display(
            "source",
            audio.audioVisualizerHtml(
                options = AudioVisualizerOptions(
                    initialDurationSeconds = minOf(projectionDuration, duration),
                    syncGroup = sync,
                ),
            ),
        )

        val jobs = [
            tracked("emotion2vec", emotion2VecEmbeddingAnalysis(region)),
            tracked("WavLM Base+", wavlmBasePlusEmbeddingAnalysis(region, layer = 6)),
        ]
        CompletableFuture.allOf(*jobs.toTypedArray()).thenApply { jobs.map { it.join() } }
    }
    .thenCompose { results ->
        val previews = results.map { result ->
            client.speechEmbeddingSmileTsnePreview(
                result,
                maxFrames = 600,
                startSeconds = projectionStart,
                durationSeconds = projectionDuration,
                poolMillis = projectionPoolMillis,
                hopMillis = projectionHopMillis,
                dimensions = 4,
                distance = SmileMdsDistance.COSINE,
                perplexity = 30.0,
                seed = 184921L,
                previewPoints = 1800,
            )
        }
        CompletableFuture.allOf(*previews.toTypedArray()).thenApply { previews.map { it.join() } }
    }
    .thenAccept { previews ->
        display(
            "speech spaces",
            speechEmbeddingPreviewDashboardHtml(
                previews,
                phaseHeight = 270,
                syncGroup = sync,
            ),
        )
    }
```

Re-running the unchanged box returns the cached neural results: source identity, exact range, model
revision, layer, chunking, MDS parameters, and preprocessing are part of the operation hash.
Change any of those inputs, or set `forceRegenerate = true`, to make a new operation. Changing a
Field-side range, pooling, sampling or distance recomputes the projection locally and leaves the
cached analysis where it is.

The settings above give 250 points across the first ten seconds: each averages 500 ms of evidence,
and a new one arrives every 40 ms, just faster than a 24 fps display. That smooths frame-level
jitter without turning the path into sparse half-second steps. Set both parameters to `null` for the
original 50 Hz vectors. Raising `maxFrames` toward the recording's full raw frame count is the one
expensive move, because an exact fit grows with the square of the point count: pool to a practical
hop, take a short exact window, or use the worker's all-frame landmark projection instead. As with
every t-SNE plot, local proximity is the evidence, and global distances, rotations and the
individual axis values are not.

## What one job records

The worker converts the selected source range to 16 kHz mono without replacing the original,
processes long recordings in overlapping contextual chunks, and stores:

- the full 50 Hz × 768 frame embedding as float16;
- raw and smoothed 20 ms WebRTC voice activity;
- frame energy in dBFS and embedding novelty;
- four worker-side classical-MDS coordinates over cosine distance for immediate previews;
- a MessagePack artifact containing the full float16 frame vectors and float64 frame times for Field;
- the pinned model revision, WavLM layer, chunking, resampling, source format, and worker revision.

`poolMillis` controls how much evidence contributes to each point; `hopMillis` independently
controls point spacing. Both round to the native 20 ms grid, and omitting them preserves the
original 50 Hz vectors. Pooling happens before `maxFrames` sampling, so changing the range, pool,
hop, dimensions, distance, perplexity, or seed never reruns either neural model. Exact MDS remains
available through `speechEmbeddingSmilePreview`; Smile's
[t-SNE](https://haifengl.github.io/manifold.html#t-sne) is the better first view for short-time local
neighbourhoods, and the worker's own projection stays as an immediate cached preview and a
provenance reference.

MDS is a navigational view, not the model's latent space. Its axes are specific to one operation;
do not compare coordinate 0 numerically between emotion2vec and WavLM, or between two independently
fitted recordings. Use the stored 768-dimensional vectors for retrieval or cross-recording
distance. The worker fixes eigenvector signs so an identical cached request has an identical view,
but rotations of a newly fitted corpus still have no semantic name.

See also the [general audio visualizers](visualizers.md#speech-embedding-phase-portraits) and
[beat and pitch analysis](audio_ai_analysis.md).

`poolMillis` controls how much evidence contributes to each point; `hopMillis` independently
controls point spacing. Both round to the native 20 ms grid, and omitting them preserves the
original 50 Hz vectors. Pooling happens before `maxFrames` sampling, so changing the range, pool,
hop, dimensions, distance, perplexity, or seed never reruns either neural model. Exact MDS remains
available through `speechEmbeddingSmilePreview`; Smile's
[t-SNE](https://haifengl.github.io/manifold.html#t-sne) is the better first view for short-time local
neighbourhoods, and the worker's own projection stays as an immediate cached preview and a
provenance reference.

MDS is a navigational view, not the model's latent space. Its axes are specific to one operation;
do not compare coordinate 0 numerically between emotion2vec and WavLM, or between two independently
fitted recordings. Use the stored 768-dimensional vectors for retrieval or cross-recording
distance. The worker fixes eigenvector signs so an identical cached request has an identical view,
but rotations of a newly fitted corpus still have no semantic name.

See also the [general audio visualizers](visualizers.md#speech-embedding-phase-portraits) and
[beat and pitch analysis](audio_ai_analysis.md).
